# Feature request

## Summary

The `Form` component supports a native submit button - `<button type="submit">` - but not a reset button:

```jsx
<Form onSubmit={() => console.log('submitted')}>
   <Field.Root>
     {/*  a normal Field.Control that renders an input */}
   </Field.Root>

   {/* works */}
   <button type="submit">
     Submit
   </button>

   {/* doesn't work */}
   <button type="reset">
     Reset
   </button>
</Form>
```

## Examples in other libraries

- [React Aria](https://react-spectrum.adobe.com/react-aria/Form.html#events) provides a reset button `<Form><Button type="reset" /></Form>`
- [React Hook Form](https://www.react-hook-form.com/faqs/#Howtoresettheform) supports a native reset button and also a `reset()` method via a hook

## Motivation

It's often useful to be able to discard all edits in a form and reset it to the initial values. This will could require Fields to additionally track the `initialValue`.

items.body:
# Feature request

## Summary

I'm using the NumberField component as a quantity input in a shopping cart.
To avoid sending too many HTTP requests, I use a debounce of 200ms on value change.

## Examples in other libraries

<!-- Provide a link to examples of this component or feature implemented in other libraries (if applicable).  -->

## Motivation

Problem:
The component’s built-in `START_AUTO_CHANGE_DELAY` is fixed at 400ms.
So when a user holds down the increment button:

At 200ms: debounce triggers an HTTP request (from the initial increment)

At 400ms: auto-repeat starts, causing a second value change → another HTTP request

This leads to two requests even though the user only held the button once.

Proposal:
Allow START_AUTO_CHANGE_DELAY to be set via props, so it can be aligned with external debounce timing.

Example API:


```tsx
<NumberField startAutoChangeDelay={200} />
```

Current Workaround:
Set the debounce timeout to >= 400ms, however this introduces a less responsive UX and feels laggy.

items.title: [field] Sync controlled value changes with field state

labels.name: type: bug
labels.description: It doesn't behave as expected.

labels.name: component: field
labels.description: Changes related to the field component.

items.body:
`Field.Control` was the only Field control that ignored controlled value changes. Switch, Checkbox, Checkbox Group, Radio Group, Select, Slider, Combobox, Number Field, and OTP Field all sync through `useValueChanged` already. `Field.Control` instead drove every field concern from the DOM change event, so a value set from code had no path at all.

Two bugs followed.

**Dirty state never cleared for non-string values.** The dirty check compares the input's string value against a baseline captured from the `value` prop. With `value={5}` the baseline was the number `5`, so `"5" !== 5` held forever and `data-dirty` stayed set even after the user returned the field to its initial value. Array values failed the same way by reference. The control now registers the serialized value, so the baseline and the comparison agree.

**Programmatic changes left the field stale.** Setting the value from code, such as a clear button or a form library reset, updated the input text but not filled, dirty, or validity, so a resolved error stayed visible and a pending async validator for the old value could still publish.

The fix gives each mode one owner instead of running two sync paths at once. `useValueChanged` owns the controlled path, `onChange` owns the uncontrolled path, and `onChange` returns early when controlled. `Field.Control` now has the same shape as its siblings, with the residual difference being the mount-time DOM read that its uncontrolled mode requires.

Two smaller fixes ride along:

- `details.cancel()` in `onValueChange` now stops the internal handling. It was ignored.
- A controlled value the consumer rejects or rewrites no longer reaches the field state, matching Combobox, Number Field and OTP Field.

## Performance

Renders per keystroke for a controlled input, counted in jsdom (mount, then four keystrokes):

| Validation mode | Base | This PR | Number Field |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `onSubmit` | 1 per keystroke | 2 on the first, then 1 | 2 on the first, then 1 |
| `onChange` | 1 per keystroke | 2 per keystroke | 2 per keystroke |

Moving the work into a layout effect costs one extra render per keystroke in `onChange` mode. That is the cost every sibling control already pays, and `Field.Control` now matches Number Field exactly. The base column achieved one render by doing the work synchronously in the change handler, which is the second sync path this PR removes.

items.body:
In a multiple Select inside a Field, `[data-dirty]` stayed set after the selection returned to its initial value.

## Root cause

The dirty check used `value !== validityData.initialValue`. In multiple mode `value` is a fresh array on every change, so the reference comparison was always true once the user interacted — even after deselecting and reselecting back to the initial items.

## Changes

- Compare array values element-by-element via `isItemEqualToValue` when computing dirty state in multiple mode, falling back to reference comparison for non-array values. This mirrors the equivalent combobox fix.
- Add regression tests for returning to the initial value, object values compared via `isItemEqualToValue`, and the order-sensitive case.

## Notes

- The comparison is order-sensitive, matching `CheckboxGroup` and `Slider`. Returning to the same items in a different order is still treated as dirty.

items.body:
> [!Tip]
> Easier to review with [hidden whitespace changes](https://github.com/mui/base-ui/pull/5423/changes?w=1)

Fixes #5422

## Summary

- Tie store mutation keys directly to their corresponding state value types.
- Propagate the same guarantee through React store synchronization and setter helpers.
- Tighten popup interaction state syncing and replace broad `Partial<State>` accumulators with exact batched updates.
- Fix invalid call sites exposed by the stricter types and add compile-time regressions.

## Root cause

`Store.set` and several `ReactStore` helpers accepted `keyof State` independently from the generic value type. TypeScript could therefore infer the value without checking it against the selected key. `Store.update` and `useSyncedValues` accepted `Partial<State>`, which allows explicitly assigning `undefined` to required fields when `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` is disabled.

Those signatures let the runtime store violate its declared state shape while selectors and component code continued to trust that shape.

Reproduction: https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitejs-vite-ghcgqkny

## Changes

- `Store.set` now accepts `State[Key]`, and `Store.update` accepts an inferred `Pick<State, Key>`.
- React store synchronization, controlled-prop, and setter helpers preserve the same key/value relationship.
- `usePopupInteractionProps` requires the common popup prop bags while validating component-specific state fields.
- Narrow floating-root synchronization to the popup-store capabilities it actually uses, preserving concrete state inference for specialized stores such as Tooltip.
- Popup, floating, and toast update paths now form exact updates while preserving batching and omitted-value behavior.
- Invalid call sites uncovered by the new types were corrected, including preventing Combobox event `type` metadata from being [merged into store state](https://github.com/mui/base-ui/pull/5423/changes#diff-30162b665077add067eff43f55765445b8292160513621f81fc186b6af941616R514-R525).
- Type-only tests cover wrong values, unknown keys, explicit `undefined`, state setters, popup interaction props, and popup open-change extra state.
- Direct tests cover the popup open-state branches that preserve active trigger data and control deferred unmounting.

## Impact

This is a breaking type change for `@base-ui/utils` consumers that pass a broad `Partial<State>` variable to `Store.update` or `ReactStore.useSyncedValues`. Existing valid object literals and exact known subsets continue to infer normally.

To migrate, represent broad partials as an exact known subset before writing them to the store. This prevents explicit `undefined` or unknown values from entering required state fields.

Store constructor initial-state parameters that still accept `Partial<State>` are deliberately out of scope for this PR and can be tightened separately.

## Validation

- `pnpm typescript`
- `pnpm eslint`
- `pnpm prettier`
- `pnpm test:jsdom ReactStore --no-watch`
- `pnpm test:jsdom popupStoreUtils --no-watch`
- `pnpm test:jsdom toast/store --no-watch`
- `pnpm test:jsdom ComboboxRootContext --no-watch`
- Focused jsdom suites for Combobox, Menu/Submenu, Tooltip, Preview Card, Popover, Dialog, Toast, and floating root synchronization

labels.description: Expand the scope of the product to solve a new problem.

labels.name: component: combobox

items.body:
Whichever way I hold Combobox values and items, it feels that in real world usage like I either need to 
- have per object ID lookups
- or, create interim objects and deal with object equality
- or, look up the object corresponding to my app's current ID value

Ideally I'd like to be able to:
- Provide `items={objectsArray}` for rendering rich design per item using info inside the objects
- Use object IDs as `value` both for `<Combobox.Root>` and `<Combobox.Item>` to retrieve/set data from/into my app 

I was surprised that something like this doesn't work as expected:
https://stackblitz.com/edit/akhn9tcs?file=src%2FApp.tsx

In the above example, if I provide `isItemEqualToValue={(item, value) => item.id === value}`:
- Initial highlight starts working correctly
- Selected item is no longer works correctly
- TS thinks `item` and `value` are both strings, so it errors on `item.id`

---

## Current approaches

Consider a simple object shape like
```ts
interface User {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  role: string;
  email: string;
  avatarUrl: string;
}
```

If providing just IDs as items, I need to build or look up a user object here to display all the info:

```jsx
<Combobox.Root items={userIds} value={currentUserId} onValueChange={userId => ... }>
  <Combobox.List>
    {(userId) => (
      <Combobox.Item value={userId}>
       {/* Need to build or look up the user object to use its fields */}
      </Combobox.Item>
     )}
  </Combobox.List>
</Combobox.Root>
```

If providing the entire object as item value, I need to either do a lookup in the object array to set the Root value, or to assemble this object on the fly (potentially unnecessary, would also have to deal with object equality)

```jsx
// Need to build or look up `currentUser`
<Combobox.Root items={users} value={currentUser} onValueChange={user => ... }>
  <Combobox.List>
    {(user) => (
      <Combobox.Item value={user}>
        ...
      </Combobox.Item>
     )}
  </Combobox.List>
</Combobox.Root>
```

Both examples above look simple but in real product with grouping and custom filtering complexity snowballs a lot

This would have been ideal

```jsx
<Combobox.Root items={users} value={currentUserId} onValueChange={userId => ... }>
  <Combobox.List>
    {(user) => (
      <Combobox.Item value={user.id}>
        ...
      </Combobox.Item>
     )}
  </Combobox.List>
</Combobox.Root>
```

items.body:
## Summary

Fixes #4951.

A store created via `createHandle` outlives the `Root` that mounts it. When a `Root` unmounted while the popup was open (for example, by navigating away), the open-cycle state (`open`/`mounted`/active trigger, plus store-specific metadata such as the open reason and transition type) stayed in the handle-owned store. When a new `Root` later adopted the same handle (navigating back), it inherited that stale state — leaving the popup stuck open, or rendering no popup while still locking the page.

This makes adopting a handle-owned store behave like creating an internal store (which is recreated on each `Root` mount): when a new `Root` adopts the handle, the open-cycle state is reset to that `Root`'s initial state. Nothing is reset on unmount itself — state written while no `Root` is mounted (e.g. by a pending hover timer) is also cleared on the next adoption.

## Details

- Adds a shared `useAdoptedStoreReset` hook in `utils/popups`, used by `usePopupStore` (Dialog, Popover, Tooltip, Preview Card) and by `MenuStore.useStore` (which bypasses `usePopupStore`).
- The reset replaces the state object directly during the adopting `Root`'s render, so the `Root` and its children never render the stale open state — a reset performed in a layout effect was tried first and produced a transient mount of the stale-open popup followed by a visible close transition, because effects registered after the reset write their stale render-computed values (such as `mounted`) back into the store.
- The replacement is idempotent and re-runs on every render until the adoption commits, so a render discarded by React (StrictMode double render, interrupted/suspended render) neither loses the reset nor consumes it prematurely. Subscribers (e.g. detached triggers that stay mounted) are notified once, in a layout effect after the adoption commits.
- Resetting to the `Root`'s initial state (rather than a hardcoded closed state) keeps `defaultOpen` intact; the controlled `open`/`triggerId` props are re-applied via `useControlledProp`.
- Beyond the base open-cycle fields (`open`/`mounted`/`transitionStatus`/active trigger/`payload`/`preventUnmountingOnClose`), each concrete store passes its own open-cycle metadata to reset through an `ADOPTION_RESET_STATE` object (the hook's `additionalResetState` argument). These are fields read during the adopting `Root`'s first render, or only re-derived by a later layout effect, so an initially open adoption (`defaultOpen` or controlled `open`) does not commit once with the previous open cycle's values:
  - **Dialog / Drawer / Alert Dialog:** `openMethod`, `nestedOpenDialogCount`, `nestedOpenDrawerCount`
  - **Popover:** `openMethod`, `openChangeReason`, `instantType`, `stickIfOpen`
  - **Tooltip:** `openChangeReason`, `instantType`, `isInstantPhase`
  - **Preview Card:** `instantType`
  - **Menu:** `activeIndex`, `allowMouseEnter`, `hoverEnabled`, `openChangeReason`, `instantType`, `stickIfOpen`, `openMethod`

  A reminder on `PopupStoreState` documents that any new open-cycle state must either be added to the reset or be re-derived by a `Root` effect.
- Popover's `Root` now disposes the timer on the store it actually uses (`store.disposeEffect()` rather than only the internal store), so a pending patient-click (`stickIfOpen`) timer scheduled on a handle-owned store is cleared when the `Root` unmounts and cannot fire into the next adoption.
- Trigger registrations are untouched; active-trigger fields are reset and re-derived from the still-mounted triggers.

## Testing

Regression tests added for all five handle-capable components, under a shared "resetting handle-owned state when a new Root adopts the handle" suite:

- **Dialog:** uncontrolled remount; controlled remount asserting no transient close cycle (via `onOpenChangeComplete`); `defaultOpen` preserved across the remount; a still-mounted detached trigger notified on adoption (StrictMode); a parent holding `open=true` across the remount; and a render-phase probe that the adopting `Root` never reads a stale nested dialog/drawer count (`it.each(['dialog', 'drawer'])`).
- **Popover:** uncontrolled remount; a hover timer firing while no `Root` is mounted; the patient-click (`stickIfOpen`) timer being cleared on unmount; and (Chromium-only) a `defaultOpen` modal `Root` locking scroll after adopting a hover-opened handle, guarding the `openChangeReason` reset.
- **Menu:** uncontrolled remount; the previously highlighted item not being restored after a remount; and a render-phase probe that a `defaultOpen` adopting `Root` never reads stale `hoverEnabled`/`openMethod`/`stickIfOpen`/`instantType`/`openChangeReason`.
- **Tooltip:** uncontrolled remount, and a render-phase probe that a `defaultOpen` adopting `Root` never reads a stale `isInstantPhase`/`instantType`.
- **Preview Card:** uncontrolled remount.

The new tests fail without the fix; the `defaultOpen` and parent-held `open=true` cases guard the fix's preservation behavior rather than the original bug. `pnpm typescript`, `pnpm eslint`, and `pnpm prettier` pass. The full Dialog/Popover/Tooltip/Preview Card/Menu suites pass in jsdom, and all `detached-triggers` suites pass in Chromium.

items.body:
Part of the Codex sweep. Ports the Select autofill and selected-state fixes (#4934) to Combobox, with the review findings from that port folded in.

## Changes

- Browser autofill matches an item's rendered label, not just its serialized value, so a primitive `value="US">United States` autofills correctly. Works for inline children and the `items` prop.
- Field state (dirty, validation, error clearing) runs through the shared `useValueChanged` effects and respects `onValueChange`/`onInputValueChange` cancellation. A canceled autofill, selection, or input change no longer touches field state, and a canceled single selection keeps the popup open.
- Multiple mode clears `data-dirty` when the value returns to its initial set, comparing element-by-element with the item comparator instead of by array reference.
- When the input is inside the popup, the trigger's `aria-controls` points at the dialog popup (a stable `${rootId}-popup` id shared by the popup and trigger) instead of the listbox.
- `Combobox.Label` resolves to `Combobox.Label.State` in the generated docs.

## Original findings addressed

- Canceling a single-select item press still closed the popup; it now stays open, with a test.
- The `${rootId}-popup` id was built in both the popup and the trigger; it's now one `getComboboxPopupId` helper, with the custom-id path covered.
- The autofill `forceMounted` mount was sticky and ran for `multiple` and `none` modes that never match; it's now scoped to single-selection autofill.

items.body:
# Get help
Summary


Base UI Input (which renders Field.Control) triggers React state updates on each keystroke (setDirty, setFilled), causing the input component/subtree to re-render continuously while typing. This happens even when the input is used in an uncontrolled way via React Hook Form register.

This makes Base UI Input hard to use in performance-sensitive forms, because RHF’s usual “uncontrolled input = minimal rerenders” benefit is lost.

Expected behavior


When using an uncontrolled input (no value prop, only ref/onChange/onBlur from RHF register), typing should not force React re-renders of the input subtree on every keystroke unless the consumer explicitly opts into controlled state or subscriptions.

Actual behavior


Typing into Base UI Input triggers re-renders on every keystroke.

## Ask a question

Request / questions

items.body:
# Bug report

## Current behavior

`Field` does not validate the initial value and the validation is inconsistent and incorrect.

With this code:

```tsx
<Field.Root>
  <Field.Label>Email</Field.Label>
  <Field.Control type="email" defaultValue="not_an_email@" />
</Field.Root>

<Field.Root>
  <Field.Label>Email</Field.Label>
  <Field.Control type="email" value="not_an_email@" />
</Field.Root>
```

The root `div` initially has only `data-filled`. When I focus then blur without typing anything, it gets `data-valid`. But if I type something (to make it dirty) and revert back to old value, it gets `data-invalid`. The `input` always has `:invalid` pseudo-class in these scenarios.

## Expected behavior

- `Field` should validate the initial value (I'm not sure if this behavior is intended or not).
- The validation should be consistent between dirty value and non-dirty value.

## Base UI version

v1.0.0-alpha.8

Chrome

-   [Built-in import support](https://tailwindcss.com/blog/tailwindcss-v4#built-in-import-support) — no additional tooling necessary to bundle multiple CSS files.

-   [CSS theme variables](https://tailwindcss.com/blog/tailwindcss-v4#css-theme-variables) — all of your design tokens exposed as native CSS variables so you can access them anywhere.
-   [Dynamic utility values and variants](https://tailwindcss.com/blog/tailwindcss-v4#dynamic-utility-values-and-variants) — stop guessing what values exist in your spacing scale, or extending your configuration for things like basic data attributes.

-   [New 3D transform utilities](https://tailwindcss.com/blog/tailwindcss-v4#new-3d-transform-utilities) — transform elements in 3D space directly in your HTML.
-   [Expanded gradient APIs](https://tailwindcss.com/blog/tailwindcss-v4#expanded-gradient-apis) — radial and conic gradients, interpolation modes, and more.
-   [@​starting-style support](https://tailwindcss.com/blog/tailwindcss-v4#starting-style-support) — a new variant you can use to create enter and exit transitions, without the need for JavaScript.
-   [not-\* variant](https://tailwindcss.com/blog/tailwindcss-v4#not-variant) — style an element only when it doesn't match another variant, custom selector, or media or feature query.
-   [Even more new utilities and variants](https://tailwindcss.com/blog/tailwindcss-v4#even-more-new-utilities-and-variants) — including support for `color-scheme`, `field-sizing`, complex shadows, `inert`, and more.

Start using Tailwind CSS v4.0 today by [installing it in a new project](https://tailwindcss.com/docs/installation/), or playing with it directly in the browser on [Tailwind Play](https://play.tailwindcss.com/).

For existing projects, we've published a comprehensive [upgrade guide](https://tailwindcss.com/docs/upgrade-guide) and built an [automated upgrade tool](https://tailwindcss.com/docs/upgrade-guide#using-the-upgrade-tool) to get you on the latest version as quickly and painlessly as possible.

For a deep-dive into everything that's new, [check out the announcement post](https://tailwindcss.com/blog/tailwindcss-v4).
